solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suffered humiliation, as woman has in Oman

parts.note: the word woman, stripped of its opening letter (its face), turns into the country name Oman

explanation.surface: Someone was humiliated, just as a woman can be in a conservative Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic reading: 'face' is the front of a word, so the woman who has lost her first letter has become Oman.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose face is the idiom for being humiliated or losing standing in others' eyes.

clue.text: After a couple of tip-offs, preventing illegal session in bar

indicators.note: two tips, one at each end, are taken off the word

parts.note: preventing something is blocking it

explanation.surface: Police, tipped off twice, stop an illegal drinking session in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip-offs' looks like police informants but means the two end letters come off BLOCKING.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock-in is after-hours drinking in a British pub with the doors locked, outside licensing hours.

clue.text: Buying spiritual benefits, perhaps, like Saint Peter originally?

parts.note: the apostle Peter was called Simon before Jesus renamed him
the suffix -y means like or having the quality of, as in silky

explanation.surface: A question whether trading in sacred favours is something the first apostle might do.
explanation.walkthrough: The name actually comes from Simon Magus, who tried to buy the apostles' power; Simon Peter is a different Simon.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony is the sin of paying for church offices or sacraments, trading in holy things.

clue.text: Cause of liver rot initially foxed physician

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: St Luke the evangelist is called 'the beloved physician'

explanation.surface: A doctor was baffled by what had caused a patient's liver to rot.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver fluke is a parasitic flatworm that causes liver rot in sheep and cattle.

clue.text: Somewhat gauche? A penny lower in value

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Is it a bit clumsy to offer a penny? Doing so makes something seem worth less.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheapen is to reduce something's worth or price, to devalue it.

clue.text: Liveliness of film describing childless state

indicators.note: describing is used in its sense of drawing a line round something, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial
SP stands for sine prole, Latin for without issue, used in genealogies
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: A film reviewer praises the energy of a movie portraying a couple who have no children.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (sine prole, 'without offspring') is a genealogist's abbreviation many solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is borrowed from French for wit and vivacity, a sprightly liveliness of mind.

clue.text: Standing Scotsman up? It might show what page you're on

definitions.text: It might show what page you're on

parts.note: standing is status or rank

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the name is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Rab is a typical Scottish man's name, short for Robert

explanation.surface: A question whether a Scot is on his feet, followed by a hint about books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'page' suggests a book, but it is a web page; the bar is a screen element.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser or app strip at the screen's edge can display the current page or document state.

clue.text: Reduced fare, using this bar at club?

parts.note: a rail is a bar, such as a towel rail
a club is one of the four suits, so a club is a playing card

explanation.surface: A drinker gets cheap prices by using this card at a club bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A British railcard gives discounted train travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A railcard is a pass entitling its holder to discounted train tickets.

clue.text: Caught up with three playing in concert

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to have got someone is to have caught them

indicators.note: playing says the letters are played about with

explanation.surface: A latecomer catches up with three musicians who are playing at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GOT into TOG; 'playing' rearranges THREE as ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting jointly, at the same time and in agreement.

clue.text: One way of meeting others to work out detailed movement of red giant

indicators.note: read as de-tailed: the final letter is cut off the word before it

parts.note: to work out a sum is to compute it

indicators.note: movement says the letters of the following words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: An astronomer sets out to calculate the precise motion of a large red star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' drops the last letter of COMPUTE, leaving COMPUT; 'movement of' shuffles RED GIANT into ERDATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching people by computer was an early form of introduction service for those looking for romantic partners.

clue.text: See 9
Film director by river, topless

indicators.note: topless in a down clue removes the first letter, the top

parts.note: the Arno is the river that flows through Florence

explanation.surface: A film director is seen sunbathing topless beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1962 film was the first James Bond movie.

clue.text: Hot new goalie, one reportedly denying Jesus room on his first appearance

definitions.text: one reportedly denying Jesus room on his first appearance

parts.note: something hot is fashionable, or in
a goalie is a goalkeeper, or keeper

explanation.surface: A talented new goalkeeper is described, then the clue swerves to the Nativity.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition retells the Nativity: in Luke's gospel there was no room at the inn, so tradition has an innkeeper turning Mary and Joseph away.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlord of the inn in the Christmas story is the figure said to have refused lodging to the holy family.

clue.text: In Paris, a piece of meat not mixed with stuff of inferior quality

definitions.text: not mixed with stuff of inferior quality

parts.note: the French for a is un
a cut is a piece of meat from a butcher

explanation.surface: A French butcher offers a piece of meat that has not been bulked out with cheaper fillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncut describes drugs or drink not diluted or adulterated with something cheaper.

clue.text: Sadly Boris Johnson is lacking direction, according to playwright

indicators.note: sadly says the letters that follow end up in a sorry, jumbled state
lacking says the word is is missing from the name before it

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A political sketch: the former Prime Minister has lost his way, in a playwright's judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes IS out of BORIS JOHNSON; add E and 'Sadly' rearranges the eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Look Back in Anger was one of Britain's 'angry young men' dramatists of the 1950s.

clue.text: A Hopi goes swimming in some of our canals

definitions.note: plural: we each have one such canal

indicators.note: swimming says the letters move around freely

explanation.surface: A Native American goes for a swim in the waterways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canals' suggests waterways; these are anatomical tubes.
explanation.definitionFit: The gullet is the alimentary canal carrying food to the stomach, and each person has one.

clue.text: See 14
Reckons using a daybook

parts.note: split as day and book: D abbreviates day, and Judges is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone works out sums with the help of a diary or account book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daybook' splits into day and book.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjudge is to deem or consider formally, close to judging or reckoning.

clue.text: Poet's written about heading missing from police flyers

indicators.note: written about says the first piece is set around the second

parts.note: a bard is a poet; with the 's the word gains a final S

indicators.note: the word below loses its first letter, its heading

parts.note: the fuzz is slang for the police

explanation.surface: A poet has written about leaflets that the police have lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyers' suggests leaflets; the definition means birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Buzzards are broad-winged birds of prey, so they are flyers.

clue.text: Once ready, German chum set off in Dutch boat

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: an ark is a boat, as in Noah's

indicators.note: off signals the letters are set off, disordered

explanation.surface: A German friend sets sail in a Dutch vessel once he is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for cash (ready money), so 'Once ready, German' is former German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Deutschmark was West Germany's currency until the euro replaced it, so it is past cash.

clue.text: Set the date? Not oddly the 5th

indicators.note: not oddly means taking the even letters, rejecting the odd ones

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to fix the date as the fifth, and is told not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb about fixing a date; it is a television set.
explanation.definitionFit: High-definition television names a type of TV set, so a set is an example of it.

clue.text: See 19
Male in uniform, at the wheel

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A man in uniform is driving.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew is a boy's name, so a male.

clue.text: Arab is tricky enemy, on paper

indicators.note: on in a down clue says one piece sits on top of the next
tricky suggests the word is twisted around

parts.note: the i is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: An Arab is described as an awkward enemy in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yemeni comes from Yemen, an Arab country in the south of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Main setter possibly clues Ancient Mariner?

parts.note: the main is the open sea
a setter is a breed of dog, so a dog possibly

explanation.surface: The puzzle's chief compiler gives hints about Coleridge's famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the crossword compiler but is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sailor with years at sea is called by this salty nickname.

clue.text: Urban outskirts? Nothing is open

indicators.note: the outskirts of the word are its outside letters

parts.note: zip is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is open on the edge of town, a lament about suburban shops.
explanation.definitionFit: To unzip a bag or jacket is to open it by undoing its zip fastener.

clue.text: Four vacuous articles about adult conversation held in private

indicators.note: about says the emptied articles wrap round the letter for adult
Four asks for the pair of articles twice over, four in all
vacuous means empty, so each article loses its inside letter

parts.note: the is the definite article; two of them here, doubled by Four
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grammarian complains of four empty articles in an adult's private chat.
explanation.walkthrough: THE emptied is TE; four of them give TETETETE, and 'about' puts A in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tete-a-tete, French for head-to-head, is an intimate talk between two people alone.

clue.text: A letter-writer reportedly in shock

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is given as spoken, P-pal

parts.note: a pen pal writes letters to a distant friend

explanation.surface: Someone writing letters is said to be in a state of shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen pal said quickly is heard as 'P-pal'.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to horrify or dismay them.

clue.text: One that might be barking mad is upset with NHS GP here, outside emergency room

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters sit around the emergency room piece
upset says the letters of the words around it are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who is barking mad is upset to find their GP outside the emergency room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking mad' tempts the solver, but 'mad' is fodder and 'barking' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed is a large working dog, and dogs bark, so it is one thing that might be barking.

clue.text: See 27
Bird seen by one in small hide

indicators.note: in says the numeral for one goes inside the small hide

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a bird while sitting alone in a small hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I between S and SKIN; the birdwatcher's hide is really an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch.

clue.text: Place of residence of daughter: area of London once in Kent

parts.words: area of London once in Kent
parts.note: Welling, now in the borough of Bexley, belonged to the county of Kent before Greater London absorbed it

explanation.surface: A daughter's home is given as a London suburb that used to lie in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county south-east of London; Welling moved into London in 1965.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling is a house or home, any place where someone lives.
